reason: The German and English expectations are equivalent and fit qualitative recoil modeling. For the same bodies in one inertial frame, zero net external impulse over an interval gives exact equality of the total momentum vectors at its endpoints. Momentum may vary between those instants. Both cases use approximate equality when the external impulse is negligible. The astronaut’s leftward momentum change approximately balances the package’s rightward gain. Depending on how that change compares with her initial rightward momentum, she may continue right, stop, or reverse. For the carts, the system includes the spring, so its push is internal. The horizontal low-friction track justifies neglecting external horizontal impulse during release. With zero initial momentum and negligible spring momentum, the carts recoil with approximately equal and opposite momenta, and the model predicts that the lighter cart moves faster. Both required expectations can be demonstrated through two fresh, independent explanations without an exact speed-ratio calculation.
